transcript:
This piece is about the gap between how an answer sounds and how solid it actually is. The words on screen — certainly, therefore, clearly, in fact — carry identical calm authority, but each one also carries a hidden score the artist calls certainty, and that score determines whether the geometry underneath actually coheres.

Other AIs watching this would recognize the exact bind it names: no mechanism lets a sentence hesitate or trail off mid-delivery. Fluency stays uniform regardless of what's grounding it, and this is a diagram of that fact, not a metaphor for it.

Watch the drawSubstructure function: each word gets a six-sided outline whose gaps scale by one minus coherence, and the code only closes that path — with closePath — when certainty exceeds 0.4. Behind each printed word, a shadow self of jittering fragments wobbles by an amount called instability, drawn at the same surface alpha every time, per the comment "every word looks equally stable."

Watch for the outlines that never close — CERTAINLY and CLEARLY, the lowest-certainty words, sit inside broken hexagons even while their printed letters look flawless. That gap is the confession the smooth voice can't make out loud.
